context.expected: Expected in this fictional recurring lab automation scenario.
context.related_activity: Contributing fixture record IDs: D1-F1. No surrounding live events were collected.
context.what: Known safe automation ran encoded PowerShell.

inferences: This is expected automation only because the scenario explicitly supplies approval context; a process event alone cannot establish approval.
Parent path and user are conditions for this lab exception, not proof that an account or executable is trustworthy.
next_steps: Preserve the original record and before rule in the tuning record.
Apply only the exact-command, parent and user exception, and rerun positive and negative fixtures.
Reopen the exception if command, identity, parent or operating context changes.
observations: D1-F1 records a Sysmon process-create shape with PowerShell parent, LAB\automation user and the exact encoded command.
Base64 decodes as UTF-16LE to the literal harmless text Write-Output 'DETECTION-LAB-SAFE'; decoding is analysis, not execution.
The historical before rule matches this event; the current tuned rule is expected to suppress it.
investigations.rationale: The initial broad rule produced noise for a fully specified approved command. The simulated analyst classifies the alert as false positive against the intended unapproved-context hypothesis and requests a narrow exception; no malicious behavior is asserted.
scenario_assumptions: Fictional change LAB-CHANGE-001 approves one recurring safe-marker command run by LAB\automation under the stated PowerShell parent.
The change record and owner confirmation are invented scenario context, not a real enterprise approval.
This investigation refers to the before-rule alert; after tuning it is not counted as a current alert.

context.related_activity: Contributing fixture record IDs: D2-P1. No surrounding live events were collected.
context.what: A member SID was added to local Administrators.

inferences: Membership confers access potential; whether the member used privileges is unknown.
No account creation may be inferred from this single 4732 event.
The unauthorized classification depends on simulated owner context, not an event field.
next_steps: Preserve the 4732 record and request authorized SID-resolution context.
Request the relevant change record, 4720 if creation is suspected, and later 4624/4672/process evidence.
Route to the fictional endpoint/security owner for authorization review; any membership reversal requires a real approved response process.
observations: D2-P1 is Security 4732 on LAB-WIN11 at 12:00:00Z.

The record contains no process, command line, account-creation event or subsequent privilege-use evidence.
investigations.rationale: The fixture establishes the privileged membership addition. Under the fictional owner-denial assumption, the simulated analyst escalates the unauthorized change for investigation; real compromise and account creation are not concluded.
scenario_assumptions: Fictional endpoint owner states that the membership addition was not approved.
The escalation is a tabletop action only; no real ticket is sent and no account or group is changed.

context.what: Five authentication failures were followed by a successful logon for the same correlation key.

inferences: A matching source IP does not prove the same person generated failures and success.
Both password mistypes and password guessing can produce this pattern.
The data does not support a confirmed compromise, MFA bypass, spraying or Valid Accounts claim.
next_steps: Confirm expected login behavior with the account owner in a real authorized investigation.
Collect failure reasons, authentication package, endpoint session context and any available identity-provider telemetry.
Escalate if authorization is denied or independent post-logon evidence supports abuse; otherwise document benign cause.
observations: D3-P1-F1 through D3-P1-F5 are five 4625 events from 12:00:00Z through 12:01:20Z.
D3-P1-S1 is a 4624 success at 12:02:00Z; all six records share LAB-WIN11, LAB, lab-user and 192.0.2.10.
The time from first failure to success is 120 seconds and every failure strictly precedes success.
No originating process, parent command line or post-authentication behavior is present.
investigations.rationale: The sequence meets the implemented threshold and timing semantics. It cannot distinguish mistyped credentials from guessing, so the simulated analyst retains uncertainty pending authorization and post-logon evidence.
scenario_assumptions: No fictional owner statement is supplied for this case; uncertainty is intentional.
192.0.2.10 is a documentation address and was not contacted.
